Whether an arm replaces (s3) as the H5 candidate is Eleonora's decision on the page's evidence. Amendments made after a number was computed would be listed in `amendments`; there are none.
ruling: Eleonora, 26 October 2026, relayed: ledger item 52, option 1 on avenue #1213 (#1215 has merged, so the quarter-end and IORB twCRPS rows can be read). Base: (s3) of #1145, the candidate; comparators (s3) and (a). At most two arms, declared before any score, calendar at the target day on direct pairs: (s3-hw1) Huber downweighting on ordinary target rows only, calendar target rows keep full weight; (s3-hw2) calendar rows get their own Huber threshold at k times the ordinary one, k = 2 (declared; one value, not tuned). hypothesis: H5 (primary goal): the SOFR - IORB spread distribution in bp. Step 3 (fix; calendar first; refocus). Development tier
target: spread_bps at the scored day, in basis points, as a 23-quantile distribution at each lead h = 1..5 (scoring_protocol.GRID)

base.name: (s3) of #1145: sc_s3_robust, the H5 candidate; comparator (a): spread_mr_fhs_mad20_f0.5 (#941)
base.module: repo_model.spread_mr_state_calendar (#1145), unchanged for (a) and (s3); the two arms of this study are two new StateArm constants (HW1, HW2) of the same module, which add one field to StateArm (calendar_k) and one optional argument to the Huber routine (a per-row multiplier of the threshold); no other estimator. tests/test_spread_mr_s3_huber_calendar.py pins that each arm is (s3) with that one setting changed, that with no calendar row inside the cut an arm is (s3) exactly, and that the arms of #1145, #1172 and #1196 are unchanged
base.formula: as (s3): q_p(t+h) = level + phi^k * (last - level) + scale(anchor) * (shift_h(T) + z_h,p), shift_h(T) = sum_j beta_j x_j(T) in scale units, z_h,p the 23 empirical quantiles of the standardised residual left after the terms; scale(r) = max(0.5, 1.4826 * median of the 20 absolute daily changes ending at r); phi, level, the two-year training window, the minimum of 60 pairs and the refit every 21 decision days are the base model's. Only the weights of the Huber fit that estimates beta_j change
base.pairs: direct (training_pairs = 'direct'), every term read at the target day. The estimation routine is decorated with repo_model.one_step_guard.guard_one_step_fit: on direct pairs it needs no allow-list entry. No entry is added to one_step_guard.ONE_STEP_ALLOW_LIST

terms.definition: #1145's, unchanged: month_end, quarter_end, tax_date, settlement_coupon, settlement_bill, dom_19_23 and post_month_end_window in all three of (s3), (s3-hw1) and (s3-hw2); no FOMC or IORB term and no state interaction. Each is a 0/1 flag of the target row, read at the target day on direct pairs; a scheduled field is read only where asof rule 2 admits it (settlements at lead 1 only)
terms.min_flagged: a term enters a lead's fit only if at least 3 of that lead's training pairs carry its flag; otherwise its effect is 0 at that refit and lead (#1115's rule)

calendar_rows.definition: a training pair's target row is a CALENDAR ROW when it carries any of: month_end (the last two business days, as the term table has it), quarter_end, tax_date, settlement_coupon, settlement_bill, fomc_day, iorb_window (each as TermTable.day_types reads it, the lead-1 reading), or a turn label of the month-end record in force since #1161 (repo_model.turn_days.turn_label: turn, quarter_end_turn, year_end). These are the types the directive lists (turn types, tax date, FOMC, IORB window, settlements). dom_19_23 and post_month_end_window are terms of the fit but are not named by the directive and are too broad to name a calendar row (the first covers about a quarter of all days), so a row that carries only one of them is ordinary for the weights. Any other row is ordinary
calendar_rows.read_from: the target row alone, by repo_model.spread_mr_state_calendar.calendar_row, which raises LookAheadError for a row after the decision's anchor: a training pair's target is on or before the anchor, so its type is already public, and the type is a weight of a past row, not an input of the forecast. The forecast reads no new field
calendar_rows.question_for_eleonora: whether the two broad windows should count as calendar rows, and whether the month-end term's two-day flag and the turn record's labels should both name a calendar row (they do here, as a union), is her call; this study declares one reading and does not try another

arms.name: sc_s3_robust
arms.role: (s3) (s1) with a Huber fit and a heavier ridge; the H5 candidate; the comparator

arms.name: sc_s3_hw1
arms.role: (s3-hw1) (s3) with calendar target rows at full weight in the Huber fit

arms.name: sc_s3_hw2
arms.role: (s3-hw2) (s3) with the calendar rows' Huber threshold at 2 times the ordinary one

estimation.units: the target of every fit is y_i = r_i / scale(o_i), the standardised residual of pair i (as arm (a) defines the raw residual r_i); an effect is a number of scale units and the effect in bp on a forecast is that number times the term's regressor times scale(anchor) of the decision, read afresh each day
estimation.s3: #1145's, unchanged: Huber iteratively re-weighted least squares (start from the ridge least-squares fit; sigma = max(1.4826 * median |r - median(r)|, 1e-6), threshold 1.345 sigma, weights 1 where |r| <= c and c / |r| beyond, a weighted ridge fit, at most 50 passes, stop when no coefficient moves by 1e-8), ridge 5.0 pseudo-days on every term coefficient and none on the intercept; the intercept is dropped; the pool is the 23 empirical quantiles of the unweighted z_i = y_i - sum_j beta_j x_ij
estimation.refit: every 21 decision days with the base fit, as the base model, #1145 and #1153 do; between refits the effects, the pools and the factors are kept and last, level, k, the anchor, scale(anchor), the flags and sizes of T and the state of the decision day are read afresh
estimation.isolation: each arm against (s3) isolates the weighting of the calendar rows in the Huber fit; (s3-hw1) and (s3-hw2) differ from each other only in the calendar threshold. Nothing else changes, so a difference between an arm and (s3) is the weights
estimation.s3_hw1: (s3) with the weight of every calendar row fixed at 1 in every pass of the iteration: the threshold of a calendar row is infinite (weights 1 where |r| <= c * m and c * m / |r| beyond, m = infinity for a calendar row and 1 for an ordinary row). sigma is still computed from ALL the current residuals, calendar rows included, as in (s3), so the ordinary rows' threshold is (s3)'s; the start, the ridge, the pass cap, the stop rule and the pool are (s3)'s
estimation.s3_hw2: (s3) with m = 2 for a calendar row (k = 2, declared; a threshold of 2.69 robust standard deviations against 1.345 for an ordinary row) and m = 1 otherwise; sigma, start, ridge, cap, stop rule and pool as (s3)
estimation.no_effect_case: where no calendar row has a residual beyond the cut, both arms are (s3) exactly (tests/test_spread_mr_s3_huber_calendar.py)

references.benchmarks: B1, B1' (repo_model.b1_calendar, #960; reported beside B1 in every table, B1 stays the protocol's benchmark) and B2 of scoring protocol v1
references.pairs: each arm against (a), (s3), B1, B1' and B2; (s3) against (a), B1, B1' and B2
references.gbm: gbm_funding (#634), read from its walks only when supplied (`--walks`, the same files as #1145). The walks are a long run that stays on Eleonora's Mac (`needs-mac`) and is not run first: without them those rows are absent and the page says so

scoring.scorer: repo_model.scoring_protocol (#655), the development tier: no verdict, no registration
scoring.days: decision days with a forecast of every arm and the benchmarks, whose five targets fall on or before 2025-12-31; no day after 2025-12-31 is read; the scored days pass lockbox.require_unlocked
scoring.outcomes: the panel's spread_bps at the target day
measures: grid CRPS (23 levels), by lead and the mean over leads 1..5 (primary)
upper-tail twCRPS, weight 1{z > 0 bp}, by lead and the mean over leads (key secondary)
scoring.paired: skill = mean(d) / mean(S(benchmark)) with d = S(benchmark) - S(candidate), positive favours the candidate; scoring_protocol.paired_tests, the studentized stationary bootstrap (ruling 1), mean block 10 business days, 10,000 draws, seed 1226; two-sided 90% interval, so the lower end is the one-sided 95% bound. Both the skill interval and the studentized interval on mean d (bp) are reported for every tested row
scoring.reading: a reading is taken from the mean-d bound (Eleonora's ruling on #1009, 20 October 2026): an arm is read better than a reference when the lower end of the 90% interval of mean d is above zero, worse when the upper end is below zero, otherwise undecided. The reading the skill interval alone would give is listed beside it when it differs. Lens C's caveat (the lag-10 HAC standard error is understated about 2x after 2020) is stated on the page
scoring.politis_white: beside the block of 10, the Politis-White automatic block length (scripts/block_length_949.py politis_white, with the Patton-Politis-White correction) of the paired loss differential of each arm against (a) and, for (s3-hw1) and (s3-hw2), against (s3), pooled and within each regime, and the pooled interval at that block length (rounded to a whole number of days). Reported, never substituted for the protocol's 10
scoring.min_days: a group of fewer than 20 days is listed and not tested

calibration.measure: the share of (decision day, lead) cells whose outcome is above the model's q95 (y > q) and, beside it, at or above it (y >= q), the two hit rules of Eleonora's open question #993, with the 90% stationary-bootstrap percentile interval over cells (mean block 50 cells, 2,000 resamples, seed 1226), for each arm, (a), B1, B1', B2 and, when walks are supplied, gbm_funding; pooled, by regime and by target day type. The nominal rate is 0.05. The band coverage of the 23-level quantiles is read the same way: the share of cells whose outcome falls in the central 50% band (q25 to q75) and the central 90% band (q05 to q95), with the same interval, under both hit rules (inside the closed band, and inside the open band)

scoring.pressure_day_types: the benchmarks (B2's pools) and the mean-reversion level read the pressure-day types of the month-end turn record in force since #1161 (repo_model.turn_days.IN_FORCE is True), as every scoring entry point on main does; (a) and (s3) therefore score differently from the pages of #1145 and #1172, which were scored on the earlier labels. The arms are compared with each other and with the benchmarks in this run
scoring.named_splits: the page names the 2020 regime (251 days) and the FOMC, IORB-window and quarter-end target days, with, for (s3) and each arm, the mean score and the reading against (a) and against (s3) on the upper-tail twCRPS and on the grid CRPS; and a table of every calendar target-day type (month_end, quarter_end, tax_date, settlement, fomc_day, iorb_window, dom_19_23, post_month_end_window, calendar_days) with the same arm's reading on ordinary days printed beside each calendar-day reading
scoring.day_type_intervals: the by-day-type intervals use the current method (the days of a type resampled in date order as if consecutive, the studentized stationary bootstrap of ruling 1 on the subsequence, as in #761), labelled as such on the page. #1221 (that method) is open and #1228 (a domain estimate beside it on #1196) has not merged; if #1221 resolves before the page is reviewed, it is a re-score by a resync, not a change made here

splits.regime: SplitDeclaration.regime of the target day (metadata/evaluation_splits.json): 2018-19, 2020, 2021-23, 2024, 2025-26 (the scaled score by the regime of the decision day)
splits.target_day_type: by the target day: month_end, quarter_end, tax_date, settlement (coupon or bill settling), fomc_day, iorb_window, dom_19_23, post_month_end_window, ordinary, and calendar_days (any of them). The groups overlap; ordinary is a day with none of the flags. The flags of the day type are the ex-post readings at lead 1
splits.unit: every split is on the target day: a target day's score is the mean over the leads that forecast it and it belongs to the group of its own date; a group's days are tested as a subsequence, as in #761

term_effects.table: per term and arm, by regime: the effect in bp in force on the flagged target days, the mean over the leads that forecast the day of scale(anchor) * beta_j * x_j at the refit the forecast used (x_j the flag; 0 where the term was absent), then the mean over the regime's flagged days, with the 90% stationary-bootstrap percentile interval over those days in date order (mean block 10 flagged days, 2,000 resamples, seed 1226; no interval under 5 days). The same in scale units.
term_effects.realised: beside them, the mean over the same flagged target days of the outcome less arm (a)'s median forecast: what arm (a) missed on those days
term_effects.calendar_share: per arm with a calendar threshold, the mean over the refits and leads of the share of training pairs whose target row is a calendar row

adoption: An arm replaces (s3) as the H5 candidate only if it beats (s3) without an ordinary-day loss; that is Eleonora's decision on this page's evidence. The page tabulates the pooled skill over (s3) with its intervals, the regimes read as gain, loss and undecided on the mean-d bound, and the reading on ordinary and calendar days, and names no threshold of its own. The arms count toward the variant count (2). Nothing in this study is a verdict.
reading_rules: An arm's gain over a reference is read as present on a split when the 90% interval of mean d excludes zero on the positive side, and as a loss when it excludes zero on the negative side; otherwise as undecided. A point estimate alone is not read. The skill interval's reading is listed beside it where it differs.
A pooled figure is never read without the regime and target-day-type splits beside it; a gain pooled and a loss in 2018-19, 2021-23 or on ordinary days is reported as mixed.
Every calendar-day reading is printed with the same arm's reading on ordinary days beside it.
(s3-hw1) and (s3-hw2) against (s3) isolate the weighting of the calendar rows in the Huber fit.
Lens C's caveat is stated on the page: the lag-10 HAC standard error is understated about 2x after 2020, so an interval that excludes zero after 2020 is narrower than it should be.

The page says this is a further look at 2018-2025 after (s3) was chosen on it, aimed at (s3)'s upper-tail losses in 2020 and on FOMC days (#1187), that the arms count toward the variant count, and that the day-type intervals keep the current method (#1221 not merged).

Nothing in this study is a verdict, and the page says so. A kill applies only to a result that is not provisional; these arms read the calendar at the target day on direct pairs, so their class is not provisional. The issue declares no kill rule.
The page ends with a marked question for Eleonora with numbered options and a default: nothing is adopted and no claim changes.
questions: Whether an arm replaces (s3) as the H5 candidate is Eleonora's.
The definition of a calendar row (the `calendar_rows` section) and k = 2 for (s3-hw2) are declared choices of this study, not tuned, and open to her review.
